documents.title: Thiếu máu thiếu sắt ASH 2026
image_only_facts: p.26 NEJM-style diagram (normal vs anemia of inflammation): Fe2+ enters the enterocyte through DMT1; ferroportin exports iron; hepcidin binds ferroportin, which is internalised and degraded in the lysosome, blocking release of iron from the enterocyte (the terms DMT1 and lysosome do not appear in the text)

p.27 diagram: iron absorbed into blood binds transferrin; excess iron stored in the liver (hepatocytes); in inflammation hepcidin blocks iron release from hepatocytes, desaturated transferrin supplies less iron to developing red cells

p.43 JAMA Figure 1 'Iron Absorption, Storage, and Conservation': oral iron absorbed in duodenum and jejunum; iron lost via skin sloughing and GI tract, typically only 1-2 mg/d; hepcidin binding degrades ferroportin (FPN1)

p.50 Table 2 'Laboratory Tests for the Measurement of Iron Status in Adults' (image only): normal values iron 10-30 umol/L, transferrin saturation >16 to <45%, ferritin men 40-300 / women 20-200 ug/L, Hb men >13 / women >12 g/dL, MCV 80-95 fL, MCH 27-34 pg, reticulocyte Hb content 31.2+/-1.6 pg; IDA: TSAT <16%, ferritin <10, MCV <80; anemia of chronic disease ferritin >100; sTFR/log ferritin index >2 in IDA, <1 in ACD; columns include IRIDA, zinc protoporphyrin, Perl's staining

p.64 slide collage: hepcidin falls/rises chart - absorption drops 34% by day 3 with daily dosing; GI adverse-event rates by oral iron salt: ferrous fumarate 47.0% (n=757), ferrous sulfate 32.3% (n=3,271), ferrous gluconate 30.9% (n=572), ferrous glycine sulfate 23.5% (n=606); GI side effects cause >50% of non-adherence; ferrous sulfate absorption ~28%; iron protein succinylate does not raise hepcidin (P=0.07) and dissolves at neutral pH in duodenum, insoluble at stomach pH <3.0

p.69 JAMA algorithm: ferritin <30 ng/mL or TSAT <20% = absolute iron deficiency diagnosed; ferritin >=30 and TSAT >=20% = unlikely, repeat TSAT after overnight fast; obvious bleeding -> treat site; premenopausal female with HMB -> gynecology; no HMB -> GI evaluation (celiac serology, H. pylori, upper endoscopy, colonoscopy for lower GI symptoms or age >35-40 y); IV iron for GI malabsorption, 2nd/3rd trimester pregnancy, oral intolerance; reassess iron stores ~4 weeks after treatment
